title: Western Art History & Asian Art (Chinese, Japanese & Indian)
subject: Arts Appreciation
description: All 14 Western art eras from Prehistoric Cave Art to Modern & Contemporary movements, plus Chinese philosophy/landscape/porcelain, Japanese aesthetics (Wabi-sabi, Ukiyo-e, Ma, Kintsugi, Zen), and Indian art & architecture.
sourceFile: Art History of Asia Chinese, Japanese, and India….docx, midterm reviewer.docx, ART APPRECIATION REVIEWER - FINAL EXAMINATION.pdf

questions.question: Famous cave painting sites such as Lascaux, Chauvet, and Altamira (created using ochre and charcoal) belong to which era?
questions.explanation: Prehistoric cave paintings (~40,000 BCE+) used natural pigments like ochre and charcoal to depict animals, humans, and symbols.

questions.question: Hierarchical scale, rigid composite views, symmetry, and a deep focus on pharaohs and the afterlife characterize which art tradition?
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptian art (e.g., Pyramids of Giza, Great Sphinx, Bust of Nefertiti) used hierarchical scale and symbolism for religion and the afterlife.

questions.question: In Ancient Greek sculpture, what does 'contrapposto' refer to?
options: Using strong dark-and-light contrasts in oil paint
Shifting the body's weight onto one leg to create a natural, lifelike pose
Building pointed arches with flying buttresses
Painting portraits with exaggerated facial flaws
questions.answer: Shifting the body's weight onto one leg to create a natural, lifelike pose
questions.explanation: Ancient Greek art focused on ideal beauty, proportion, and naturalism through contrapposto, alongside Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian architecture like the Parthenon.

questions.question: Which civilization is particularly known for realistic portraiture, mosaics, frescoes, and monumental public architecture like the Colosseum and Pantheon?
questions.explanation: Ancient Roman art communicated imperial power and civic life through realistic portraiture and structures like the Colosseum and Pantheon.

questions.question: Pointed arches, luminous stained glass windows, and flying buttresses are hallmarks of which Medieval architectural style?
questions.explanation: Gothic cathedrals used pointed arches, stained glass, and flying buttresses to inspire awe and teach biblical stories.

questions.question: Literally meaning 'rebirth,' the Renaissance was driven by Humanism and introduced which key visual innovations?
options: Hierarchical scale and flat stick figures
Linear perspective, naturalism, balanced proportion, and anatomical study
Random drip painting and neon plastics
questions.answer: Linear perspective, naturalism, balanced proportion, and anatomical study
questions.explanation: Renaissance masters like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo (David, Creation of Adam), and Raphael (School of Athens) revived classical ideals with perspective and anatomy.

questions.question: Dramatic movement, intense emotion, and 'chiaroscuro' (strong light-and-dark contrast) by artists such as Caravaggio, Bernini, and Rembrandt define which period?
questions.explanation: Baroque art (c. 1600–1700) sought to emotionally engage viewers through drama, dynamism, and chiaroscuro.

questions.question: Developing in France as a lighter, playful reaction to Baroque grandeur, which style favored pastel colors, ornate decoration, and aristocratic leisure scenes (Watteau, Boucher, Fragonard)?
questions.explanation: Rococo (c. 1700–1775) emphasized elegance, pastel palettes, and playful aristocratic themes.

questions.question: Drawing inspiration from ancient Greece and Rome, which movement valued order, clarity, reason, restraint, and civic virtue (exemplified by Jacques-Louis David's 'Oath of the Horatii')?
questions.explanation: Neoclassicism (c. 1760–1830) revived classical Greek and Roman discipline, symmetry, and moral clarity.

questions.question: A painting of a dramatic ocean storm that conveys fear, awe, and the overwhelming power of nature best exemplifies which movement?
questions.explanation: Romanticism (Delacroix, Turner, Friedrich) reacted against cold rationality by celebrating emotion, imagination, and the dramatic power of nature.

questions.question: An honest, unidealized painting of stone breakers or everyday peasants working in the fields (such as Gustave Courbet's 'The Stone Breakers') belongs to:
questions.explanation: Realism (c. 1830–1880) depicted ordinary people and contemporary social conditions without romantic idealization.

questions.question: Capturing fleeting visual impressions, changing sunlight, atmosphere, and visible brushstrokes (as in Claude Monet's 'Impression, Sunrise') characterizes:
questions.explanation: Impressionists (Monet, Renoir, Degas, Pissarro) focused on light, color, atmosphere, and momentary perception.

questions.question: Which early 20th-century movement, co-founded by Pablo Picasso, broke objects into geometric planes and showed multiple viewpoints simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Cubism (1907–1914) fragmented forms into geometric facets and multiple perspectives.

questions.question: Match each Modern Art movement to its defining focus and key artist:
options: Fauvism: bold non-naturalistic color (Matisse); Dada: anti-convention (Duchamp); Surrealism: dreams/unconscious (Dalí); Abstract: non-representational (Kandinsky/Pollock)
Fauvism: dreams (Dalí); Surrealism: comic books (Warhol); Dada: Greek symmetry (David)
Cubism: pastel leisure (Boucher); Expressionism: marble pharaohs; Pop Art: cave charcoal
Dada: Gothic stained glass; Abstract: chiaroscuro; Fauvism: pointillism only
questions.answer: Fauvism: bold non-naturalistic color (Matisse); Dada: anti-convention (Duchamp); Surrealism: dreams/unconscious (Dalí); Abstract: non-representational (Kandinsky/Pollock)
questions.explanation: Modern Art challenged convention across Fauvism (Matisse), Expressionism (Kandinsky), Cubism (Picasso), Dada (Duchamp), Surrealism (Dalí), Abstract (Pollock), and Pop Art.

questions.question: How does Contemporary Western Art (c. 1980–Present) often differ from older classical traditions?
options: It forbids the use of photography and video.
It often prioritizes ideas, concepts, identity, globalization, and technology over traditional beauty alone.
It strictly follows Roman architectural orders.
It restricts artists to oil on wood panel.
questions.answer: It often prioritizes ideas, concepts, identity, globalization, and technology over traditional beauty alone.
questions.explanation: Contemporary art expands traditional media to include installation, video, performance, and digital tools while exploring identity, politics, and technology.

questions.question: Which three philosophical and religious traditions most deeply shaped Chinese art?
questions.explanation: Chinese art evolved under Confucianism, Daoism, and Buddhism, emphasizing harmony with nature, discipline, and ancestral respect.

questions.question: Why do traditional Chinese landscape paintings—like Fan Kuan's 'Travelers Among Mountains and Streams'—depict tiny human figures beneath towering mountains and mist?
options: To reflect Daoist philosophy, showing humanity's humble place in harmony with vast nature
Because ancient Chinese artists did not know how to draw larger people
To imitate European Rococo garden scenes
questions.answer: To reflect Daoist philosophy, showing humanity's humble place in harmony with vast nature
questions.explanation: Daoism emphasizes harmony with nature and the natural order; monumental peaks dwarf human travelers to express this worldview.

questions.question: In Chinese visual culture, what do the dragon and the lotus traditionally symbolize?
options: Dragon: military defeat; Lotus: winter cold
Dragon: power and good fortune; Lotus: purity
questions.answer: Dragon: power and good fortune; Lotus: purity
questions.explanation: Rich symbolism in Chinese art associates dragons with power and good fortune and the lotus with purity.

questions.question: Why was the life-sized Terracotta Army created in ancient China?
options: As tourist souvenirs along the Silk Road
To guard and accompany Emperor Qin Shi Huang in the afterlife
To decorate Buddhist caves in India
To serve as props in Japanese Kabuki theater
questions.answer: To guard and accompany Emperor Qin Shi Huang in the afterlife
questions.explanation: The Terracotta Army consists of life-sized clay soldiers, horses, and chariots built for Emperor Qin Shi Huang's tomb.

questions.question: Which Chinese art form uses brush and ink to create expressive written characters where stroke quality, movement, and arrangement are prized?
questions.explanation: Chinese calligraphy is revered as a major visual art form expressing energy and balance through brushwork.

questions.question: Which indigenous Japanese belief system celebrates nature spirits called 'kami,' and which Buddhist tradition later brought meditation and minimalism to Japanese art?
questions.explanation: Japanese art blends indigenous Shinto reverence for nature (kami) with Zen Buddhist simplicity and meditation.

questions.question: An irregular, handmade tea bowl valued for its simplicity, naturalness, and signs of aging best illustrates which Japanese aesthetic concept?
questions.explanation: Wabi-sabi is the appreciation of imperfection, simplicity, impermanence, and natural aging.

questions.question: What is 'Kintsugi'?
options: Repairing broken pottery with lacquer, often highlighting the seams with gold
questions.answer: Repairing broken pottery with lacquer, often highlighting the seams with gold
questions.explanation: Kintsugi treats breakage and repair as part of an object's history rather than something to hide.

questions.question: In Japanese aesthetics, what does 'Ma' refer to?
options: A meaningful interval, pause, or emptiness between objects or events that creates calm and balance
A woodblock print of urban actors
A bright red silk kimono pattern
questions.answer: A meaningful interval, pause, or emptiness between objects or events that creates calm and balance
questions.explanation: Ma values negative space or meaningful intervals—emptiness contributes actively to balance and calm.

questions.question: What does 'Ukiyo-e' translate to, and who created its famous print 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa'?
options: 'Pictures of the floating world'; Katsushika Hokusai
'Ink of the silent mountain'; Fan Kuan
questions.answer: 'Pictures of the floating world'; Katsushika Hokusai
questions.explanation: Ukiyo-e means 'pictures of the floating world'—Japanese woodblock prints such as Hokusai's Great Wave from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

questions.question: Which pair correctly defines 'Sumi-e,' 'Ikebana,' and 'Japonisme'?
options: Sumi-e: ink wash painting; Ikebana: flower arrangement; Japonisme: Western fascination with and influence from Japanese art
Sumi-e: stone garden; Ikebana: tea bowl; Japonisme: Chinese porcelain
Sumi-e: origami; Ikebana: woodblock printing; Japonisme: Buddhist temple
Sumi-e: gold lacquer repair; Ikebana: calligraphy; Japonisme: Zen meditation
questions.answer: Sumi-e: ink wash painting; Ikebana: flower arrangement; Japonisme: Western fascination with and influence from Japanese art
questions.explanation: Sumi-e is ink wash painting, Ikebana is flower arrangement, and Japonisme is the Western artistic interest in Japanese aesthetics.

questions.question: The Ryōan-ji Rock Garden in Kyoto, composed of carefully arranged stones and raked gravel, was designed primarily to encourage:
questions.explanation: Zen dry landscape gardens (like Ryōan-ji) use minimal rocks and raked gravel to inspire contemplation.

questions.question: In Hindu sculpture, why are deities such as Shiva often depicted with multiple arms?
options: To symbolize divine attributes, powers, and spiritual roles
To show motion blur like Impressionist painting
Because sculptors followed Greek contrapposto rules
questions.answer: To symbolize divine attributes, powers, and spiritual roles
questions.explanation: Multiple arms and symbolic hand gestures (mudras) communicate divine attributes and cosmic powers rather than anatomical literalism.

questions.question: In Indian iconography, what are 'mudras'?
options: Symbolic hand gestures used in sculpture and painting to communicate spiritual meanings
questions.answer: Symbolic hand gestures used in sculpture and painting to communicate spiritual meanings
questions.explanation: Mudras are symbolic hand gestures alongside poses and attributes that convey religious teachings.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal in Agra—a symmetrical white marble mausoleum commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal—is a premier example of which architectural tradition?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal exemplifies Mughal architecture (Islamic-influenced Indian art), distinct from Nagara and Dravida temple traditions.

questions.question: Where is the celebrated Buddhist mural 'Bodhisattva Padmapani' (depicting a compassionate figure holding a lotus) located?
questions.explanation: The Bodhisattva Padmapani wall painting is one of the most famous murals of the Ajanta Caves in Maharashtra, India.

questions.question: Which ancient Buddhist dome monument with elaborate stone gateway carvings is traditionally associated with Emperor Ashoka?
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is a foundational monument of early Buddhist architecture associated with Emperor Ashoka.

questions.question: Which summary accurately contrasts the core emphasis of Chinese, Japanese, and Indian art?
options: Chinese: harmony & philosophy; Japanese: simplicity & impermanence; Indian: spirituality & religious mythology
Chinese: Gothic arches; Japanese: Mughal marble; Indian: terracotta soldiers
Chinese: asymmetry; Japanese: hierarchical scale; Indian: oil impasto
Chinese: Pop Art; Japanese: Realism; Indian: Dadaism
questions.answer: Chinese: harmony & philosophy; Japanese: simplicity & impermanence; Indian: spirituality & religious mythology
questions.explanation: Chinese art highlights harmony/nature/philosophy; Japanese art highlights simplicity/impermanence; Indian art highlights spirituality/divine narratives.

questions.question: Which pair of art terms is INCORRECTLY matched?
options: Wabi-sabi — Beauty in imperfection and aging
questions.explanation: Chiaroscuro is the Baroque strong light-and-dark contrast; the Greek column orders are Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian.

questions.question: In the big picture of Western art history, which sequence correctly orders the major eras chronologically?
options: Prehistoric -> Greek -> Medieval -> Renaissance -> Baroque -> Neoclassicism -> Romanticism -> Impressionism -> Modern
Renaissance -> Medieval -> Greek -> Baroque -> Romanticism -> Realism -> Prehistoric -> Modern
Impressionism -> Neoclassicism -> Rococo -> Renaissance -> Egyptian -> Modern
Baroque -> Renaissance -> Gothic -> Roman -> Impressionism -> Romanticism
questions.answer: Prehistoric -> Greek -> Medieval -> Renaissance -> Baroque -> Neoclassicism -> Romanticism -> Impressionism -> Modern
questions.explanation: Western art progresses chronologically from Prehistoric, Egyptian/Greek/Roman, and Medieval through Renaissance, Baroque/Rococo, Neoclassicism, Romanticism, Realism, Impressionism, Modern, and Contemporary.

questions.question: An exam describes 'classical themes, symmetry, restraint, and disciplined composition.' Which Western movement is being described?
questions.explanation: Neoclassicism values classical Greek/Roman inspiration, symmetry, order, clarity, and restraint.
